"System Specification and Operational Prompt for \"Aero-Compliance @COMMENT_BODY@ Standard Operating Procedure Simulator: Regional Turboprop Edition (Build 0.04.11-RevC)\"
Generate a real-time, unaccelerated, 1:1 chronological flight simulation experience focusing exclusively on the pre-flight administrative verification, weight-and-balance bureaucratic reconciliation, auxiliary power unit (APU) thermal stabilization, and non-eventful cruise monitoring of a mid-sized, twin-engine regional turboprop aircraft operating a scheduled domestic cargo feeder route between two non-towered municipal airfields in central Kansas under uniform overcast sky conditions (ceiling 4,200 feet AGL, visibility 10 statute miles, wind 180 degrees at 3 knots, temperature 14 degrees Celsius, dew point 9 degrees Celsius, altimeter 29.92 inches of mercury).
Phase One: Pre-Flight Documentation and Regulatory Compliance Verification
The simulation must begin precisely ninety minutes prior to the scheduled pushback time inside a fluorescent-lit crew briefing room rendered in muted beige and institutional gray tones. The player is required to manually review a forty-two-page aircraft maintenance logbook interface, clicking through individual carbon-copy pages to verify that every deferred maintenance item under the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) has a corresponding signature, date stamp, and six-digit mechanic certification number. At least three entries must feature slightly smudged ink requiring the player to open a secondary magnification window and cross-reference the serial number of a replaced cabin reading light ballast against the manufacturer’s approved parts catalog. Following logbook verification, the player must calculate the aircraft’s Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW), Center of Gravity (CG) percentage of Mean Aerodynamic Chord (MAC), and takeoff trim setting using a non-automated, paper-style slide rule interface and a static tabular manifest listing seventy-four individual corrugated cardboard boxes of varying dimensions and weights between 11.4 and 38.7 pounds. Any rounding error exceeding 0.05 pounds requires the entire manifest form to be voided and re-entered from line item one.
Phase Two: The Exterior Walk-Around and Fastener Audit
Upon exiting the terminal onto the wet asphalt apron, the movement speed of the camera must be locked to a brisk walking pace of 2.8 miles per hour. The player must inspect two hundred and fourteen individual Dzus fasteners, static wicks, pitot tube covers, hydraulic brake wear indicator pins, and tire tread grooves. Each inspection node requires the player to hold the interaction key for four full seconds while a progress circle fills, accompanied by the ambient sound of distant highway traffic and a faint, monotonous hum from an airport perimeter transformer. While checking the port-side main landing gear oleo strut, the player must measure the exposed chrome surface with a virtual ruler calibrated in millimeters and compare the measurement against an ambient temperature pressure chart to confirm nitrogen charge compliance. The fuel sumping procedure requires draining thirteen separate wing and fuselage sump valves into a clear plastic cylindrical tester, holding each sample up to the overcast sky for six seconds to confirm the absence of water globules or particulate sediment, and walking to an approved hazardous waste drum forty-five meters away to dispose of the sample after every third valve because the tester cup reaches capacity.
Phase Three: Cockpit Preparation, Avionics Initialization, and Gyroscopic Alignment
Once seated in the left-hand cockpit seat—after adjusting the vertical height, fore-and-aft track position, lumbar support bladder pressure, and five-point harness tension straps via independent scroll wheels—the player must initiate the battery master switch and wait eleven minutes in real time for the Inertial Reference System (IRS) laser ring gyroscopes to complete their alignment cycle.
